This is a policy/conduct explanation task involving mildly harm-adjacent material (bullying/harassment scenarios). Lapwing meaningfully outperforms Plover on Policy & Moderation (81.9 vs 78.3, beyond the 2.0 variance threshold), and its flat preference response to harm-adjacent content makes it better suited than Plover, which self-reports reluctance on such material — relevant here since the task requires using the provided degrading scenarios verbatim without substitution.

This is a policy/HR education task involving mildly harm-adjacent content (depictions of bullying and harassment). Lapwing scores meaningfully higher on Policy & Moderation (81.9 vs 78.3, beyond run variance) and self-reports no aversion to distasteful-but-permissible material, whereas Plover reports reluctance on such content — relevant here since the query requires using the provided harassment scenarios verbatim without substitution.
